635:
(a) All property directly connected to the sewer system and served by sewage works shall be subject to fees in support of the construction, extension, and improvement of the public sanitary sewers, to be levied and collected in accordance with subsection (f) of this section. The cost of principal and interest, either bonded or otherwise, shall be borne to those users connected to the system.
(b) The annual operating and maintenance cost of the sewer system shall be paid by the users of the system in proportion to their use. Charges for use of the system shall be based upon volume of wastewater discharged to the sewage works or the volume of water used.
(c) The city shall establish a user rate in accordance with appropriate federal and state rules and regulations pertaining to the costs associated to the use of the sewer by residential, commercial, and individual users.
(d) The city shall, in establishing the rates referred to in subsections (a) and (b) of this section, make specific reference to the sewer use rate structure in force at the time of any connection. The sewer use rate structure shall incorporate the requirements of 40 CFR 35.935-13.
(e) Rates provided for within this section shall be established by the mayor and council and may be changed from time to time as required.
(f) Users intending to connect to the public sewer shall pay an initial hookup charge which shall be established by the city and may be changed from time to time as required. These hookup charges may be used for either pre-existing, current or future capital improvements.
(g) Hookup charges as provided in this section shall be payable in full prior to the start of construction for all additions, improvements to, and/or enlargements of existing buildings, or upon the start of the construction or installation of non-building or accessory structures directly and indirectly connected to the public sewer.
(h) All sums payable to the city under this article shall be secured by a lien on all real property and improvements intended to be served by the connection for which the payment is due in the manner and to the same effect as taxes are a lien upon real estate and shall be further secured by a lien on any commercial equipment the ordinary use and operation of which generates wastewater, and a lien on any and all furnishings, fixtures and equipment used in connection with the use and operation of such commercial equipment, to the same effect as taxes are a lien upon personal property.
(i) All users authorized by the city to discharge industrial wastes, as defined by this article and discussed in section 30-52, shall be required to pay a surcharge for wastes exceeding normal wastewater concentrations. Such rates shall be subject to city treatment capacity, and shall be cumulative for each constituent exceeding normal wastewater and shall be based on the following:
(1) Industrial rate surcharges for discharges exceeding normal wastewater:
Constituent Concentration × 8.34 × Sewage Discharged × Cost per Pound
Where concentration is measured in mg/L above the normal wastewater concentration. Sewage discharged is in millions of gallons, cost per pound is in dollars and "8.34" is a constant for unit conversion. The cost per pound shall be set by the city and published separately.
(2) Sewage constituent concentrations or quantities above maximum amounts as set by the city and published separately shall be deemed a violation or shall be subject to additional surcharges as determined by and at the sole discretion of the city.
(3) Continued exceedances of normal wastewater sewage constituent concentrations or quantities may be deemed a violation or may be subject to additional surcharges as determined by and at the sole discretion of the city.
(4) No statement contained in this section shall be construed as preventing any special agreement between the city and any industrial concern whereby industrial waste may be accepted for treatment.
(Ord. No. 2018-04(2), art. 11, 4-3-2018; Ord. No. 2018-07(3), art. 11, 7-3-2018)
636:
(a) The following are considered industrial wastes and as such shall not be discharged to a public sanitary sewer, a storm sewer or a natural outlet, without first having written authorization to do so by the city, approval from all applicable regulatory agencies, and an NPDES pretreatment permit, if required.
(1) Any waters or wastes containing iron, chromium, copper, zinc, and similar objectionable or toxic substances; or wastes exerting an excessive chlorine requirement, to such degree that any such material received in the composite sewage at the sewage treatment plant exceeds the limits established by the Superintendent or the industry user's National Pollution Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) pretreatment permit for such materials.
(2) Any waters or wastes containing phenols or other taste- or odor-producing substances, in such concentrations exceeding limits which may be established by the superintendent or the industry user's NPDES pretreatment permit as necessary, after treatment of the composite sewage to meet the requirements of the state, federal, or other public agencies or jurisdiction for such discharge to the receiving waters.
(3) Any radioactive wastes or isotopes of such half-life or concentration as may exceed limits established by the superintendent or the industry user's NPDES pretreatment permit in compliance with applicable state or federal regulations.
(4) Any waters or wastes having a pH less than 5.0 or in excess of 9.5.
(5) Materials which exert or cause:
a. Unusual concentrations of inert suspended solids (such as, but not limited to, Fuller's earth, lime slurries, and lime residues) or of dissolved solids (such as but not limited to, sodium chloride and sodium sulfate).
b. Excessive discoloration (such as, but not limited to dye wastes and vegetable tanning solutions which cannot be removed by the treatment process), which consequently imparts color to the treatment plants effluent, thereby creating objectionable conditions in the receiving stream which interfere with the streams designated use.
c. BOD, chemical oxygen demand, TSS, phosphorus, fats, oils, grease, TKN, metals, volatile organic compounds or chlorine requirements in such quantities or concentrations as to constitute a significant load on the sewage treatment works, may cause the effluent limitations of the discharge permit to be exceeded.
d. Unusual volume of flow or concentration of wastes constituting "slugs" as defined herein.
(b) Waters or wastes containing substances which are not amenable to treatment or reduction by the sewage treatment processes employed, or are amenable to treatment only to such degree that the sewage treatment plant effluent cannot meet the requirements of other agencies having jurisdiction over discharge to the receiving waters.
(c) If any waters or wastes are discharged, or are proposed to be discharged to the public sewers, which waters contain the substances or possess the characteristics enumerated in subsections (a) and (b) of this section and which in the judgment of the superintendent, may have a deleterious effect upon the sewage works, processes, equipment, or receiving waters, or which otherwise create a hazard to life or constitute a public nuisance, the superintendent may:
(1) Reject the wastes.
(2) Require pretreatment to an acceptable condition for discharge to the public sewers.
(3) Require control over the quantities and rates of discharge; and/or
(4) Require payment to cover the added cost of handling and treating the wastes not covered by existing taxes or sewer charges under the provisions of section 30-51.
(d) If the superintendent permits the pretreatment or equalization of waste flows, the design and installation of the plans and equipment shall be subject to the review and approval of the superintendent, and subject to the requirements of all applicable codes, ordinances, laws and the municipal discharge permit. Further, such pretreatment installations must be consistent with and in compliance with the requirements of any state pretreatment permit issued to the industry user. The industry user shall provide the city with copies of the pretreatment permit and the monthly discharge monitoring reports upon request of the superintendent.
(e) Should it become necessary to give consideration to the contents of subsections (a) and (b) of this section, this article shall be amended accordingly, i.e., to receive and treat such industrial wastes.
(f) Sampling and testing of waters and wastes discharged to public sewers to ensure compliance with this article shall occur at the point of the connection to the public sewer. Sampling and testing shall occur during periods of industrial discharge at a minimum of every six months. If sampling is performed for compliance with state or federal permits, copies of such testing results shall be forwarded to the city. The results of the tests must give concentrations for the following constituents: BOD, TSS, TKN, P, fats, oils, grease, and any other pollutants considered significant by the city or state or federal regulators.
(g) New industry seeking to locate in the city or existing industry users proposing to expand operations in the city shall notify the superintendent of its proposal to discharge water and waste to the public sewer. Following notification, a planning meeting shall be conducted by the city for all proposed discharges greater than normal wastewater as defined in section 30-41. In the interest of the industry user, this planning meeting should be conducted by the city near the beginning of the planning phase.
(h) Any industry user that is not satisfying the requirements of the this article at the time of adoption of the ordinance from which it is derived shall within ten days submit a written explanation to the city of why it cannot comply with the provisions of this article and shall further provide a written schedule outlining its plans to obtain compliance with the provisions of this article. The city will endeavor to work in good faith with the industry user but the city will not jeopardize operation of the wastewater treatment plant and wastewater facilities.
(Ord. No. 2018-04(2), art. 12, 4-3-2018; Ord. No. 2018-07(3), art. 12, 7-3-2018)
637:
(a) The city reserves the right to terminate water and wastewater disposal services and disconnect a customer from the system when:
(1) Acids or chemicals damaging to sewer lines or treatment process are released into the public sewer causing rapid deterioration of these structures or interfering with proper conveyance and treatment of wastewater.
(2) A governmental agency informs the city that the effluent from the wastewater treatment plant is no longer of a quality permitted for discharge into a watercourse and it is found that the customer is discharging wastewater into the public sewer that cannot be sufficiently treated or requires treatment that is not provided by the city as normal domestic treatment.
(3) The customer:
a. Discharges industrial waste or wastewater that is in violation of the permit issued by the approving authority.
b. Discharges wastewater at an uncontrolled, variable rate in sufficient quantity to cause an imbalance in the wastewater treatment process.
c. Fails to pay monthly bills for sanitary sewer service when due.
d. Repeats a discharge of prohibited wastes into public sewers.
(b) Discontinuance of service for failure to comply. Failure to comply with the provisions of this article shall be cause for the discontinuance of sewer or water service to the offending person. The procedure shall be as follows:
(1) A written notice, signed by the superintendent, shall be delivered personally to the person then responsible for the offending use, outlining the conditions of the wastes which violate the city ordinances. In the event that the person in charge will not accept the notice, it shall be conveyed by registered mail to the responsible person.
(2) The person notified shall have 24 hours from the time of receipt of the notice, either personally delivered or received by registered mail, to correct the offending conditions.
(3) If correction is not made or a request for extension is not received by the city within 24 hours, it shall be mandatory that water or sewer service shall be discontinued to the offending person without further notice.
(4) If a request for an extension of time is received by the city within 24 hours of the above notice and if circumstances are such that, in the opinion of the superintendent, the best interest of the city would be served by extending the time for correction of the offending condition, then he may grant an extension of time up to a maximum limit of 30 days.
(Ord. No. 2018-04(2), art. 13, 4-3-2018; Ord. No. 2018-07(3), art. 13, 7-3-2018)
638:
The provisions of this article shall not be deemed as alleviating compliance with applicable state and federal regulations. All nonresidential users will be required to comply with pretreatment standards as outlined in 40 CFR 403.
(Ord. No. 2018-04(2), art. 14, 4-3-2018; Ord. No. 2018-07(3), art. 14, 7-3-2018)
642:

644:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accessory use means one which is:
(1) Subordinate to and serves a principal structure or use;
(2) Subordinate in area, extent, and purpose to the principal structure or use served;
(3) Located on the same lot as the principal structure or use; and
(4) Customarily incidental to the principal structure or use.
Alley means a thoroughfare either used or shown on any recorded description of the subject parcel which affords only a secondary means of access to abutting property.
Alteration of building means any addition to the height, width, or depth of a building or structure, or any change in the location of the exterior walls.
Automobile sales lot means a lot which is used principally for the storage and sale of complete and operable automobiles.
Automobile wrecking yard means a lot where three or more vehicles, not in running condition, or parts thereof, are stored, or any building or structure used principally for wrecking and storage of automobiles not in running condition.
Bed and breakfast means a house, or portion thereof, where short-term lodging, rooms, and meals are provided to the public for compensation. The operator of the bed and breakfast shall live on the premises or adjacent premises. Meals shall be provided only to individuals paying for lodging rooms. Accessory uses commonly associated with hotels and motels such as laundry services, gift shops, banquet halls, barber shops and beauty shops shall not be permitted.
Billboard means any sign or advertisement used as an outdoor display by the painting, posting, or affixing on any surface of a picture, emblem, words, figures, numbers, or letters, such sign or advertisement being remote from the point of sale.
Buffer means a portion of a lot set aside for open space and visual screening between land uses to minimize conflicts between them.
Building means a structure built, maintained, or intended for use as a shelter for persons, animals, or property of any kind. Where independent units with separate entrances are separated by common walls, each unit is a separate building. See Structure.
Building, accessory, means a building which is:
(1) Subordinate to and serves a principal structure or use;
(2) Subordinate in area, extent, and purpose to the principal structure or use served;
(3) Located on the same lot as the principal structure or use served; and
(4) Customarily incidental to the principal structure or use.
Building height means the vertical distance measured from the average established grade at the building line to the highest point of the structure.
Building, principal, means a building in which is conducted, or in which is intended to be conducted, the main or principal use of the lot on which it is located.
Building setback line means a line beyond which no foundation, wall, eave, or other part of any building shall be built, altered, or maintained, unless specified exceptions are made elsewhere in these regulations.
Club, lodge, civic, or fraternal organization means buildings and facilities owned or operated by a corporation, association, or persons for a social, educational, religious, or recreational purpose but not primarily for profit or to render a service which is customarily carried on as a business.
Conditional use means a use which is not permitted inherently but may be permitted within a zoning district. The proposed use shall not adversely affect the property values or general character of the area.
Customary home occupation means a business, profession, occupation or trade conducted for gain or support by any occupant of a dwelling and located entirely within a residential building, or a structure accessory thereto, which use is accessory, incidental, and secondary to the use of the building for dwelling purposes and does not change the essential residential character or appearance of such building.
Day nursery orday care center means a licensed and approved public or private operation, the purpose of which is to care for children in a group setting where education may be involved and meals may be served.
Dwelling means any building which is designed or used for permanent living quarters for one or more families.
Dwelling, multifamily, means a building designed for and used as a residence for three or more families, and consisting of three or more separate dwelling units.
Dwelling, single-family detached, means a dwelling designed for and occupied by not more than one family and having no roof, floor, or wall in common with any other dwelling unit.
Dwelling, two-family, means a building designed for and used as a residence for two families and consisting of two separate dwelling units. Also referred to as a duplex.
Family means one or more persons related by blood, marriage, adoptions, or guardianship and not more than five unrelated persons occupying a dwelling unit and living as a single housekeeping unit.
Frontage means the distance along which the property abuts one side of a street, roadway, highway, or right-of-way.
Garage means a building or structure used, or intended to be used, for the parking and storage of motor vehicles.
Hotel means a building or group of buildings used, or intended to be used, for the provision of daily lodging of persons for compensation.
Junkyard means any lot or structure used for a salvaging operation, including, but not limited to, the storage and sale of waste paper, scrap metal, building materials, and the collection, demolition, dismantling, storage, and salvage of automobiles or other vehicles or other machinery and parts thereof.
Land use plan means a plan consisting of proposals as to how physical development should take place in the future.
Lot means a parcel or plat of land occupied by or designated to be developed for one principal building or use and the accessory buildings or uses customarily incidental to such building, use, or development, including such open spaces and yards as designated or required by this chapter for such building, use, or development.
Lot, corner, means a lot which abuts at the intersection of two or more streets, or upon a curved street, provided that the two sides of the lot intersect to form an interior angle of not more than 135 degrees.
Lot depth means the mean distance between the front and rear lot lines, measured in the general direction of the side lot lines.
Lot frontage means the distance between the side lot lines measured at the street right-of-way line.
Lot width means the mean distance between the side lot lines measured at right angles to those side lot lines.
Mini-warehouse means a one-story building or series of one-story buildings with separate enclosed areas available for rent for the storage of personal goods.
Motel means a building or group of buildings used, or intended to be used, for the provision of daily lodging of persons for compensation, with a provision for direct vehicular access to each unit.
Nonconforming use means any building, structure, or use existing at the time of enactment of this chapter that does not conform to the regulations of the zoning district in which it is located.
Off-street loading space means the area required to load or unload goods or other materials plus the necessary driveways and maneuvering areas.
Permitted use means those uses specifically used in this chapter as special use exceptions and conditional uses subject to approval by the city council.
Public notice, as required by state law, means a notice published in the newspaper of general circulation in the city setting forth the time, place, and purpose of a public hearing on a proposed zoning decision, at least 15 days but not more than 45 days prior to the date of the hearing.
Signs. See section 32-202.
Structure means anything constructed or erected that requires location on the ground, or attached to something having a location on the ground.
Subdivision means any division or redivision of a lot, tract, or parcel into two or more lots, tracts, sites, or parts by means of mapping, plotting, conveyance, or rearrangement of boundaries.
Yard means the open, unoccupied space on the same lot with the principal building between the lot line and the building setback line.
Yard, front, means a yard extending the full width of the lot between the street right-of-way line and the front building setback line.
Yard, rear, means a yard extending the full width of the lot between the rear lot line and the rear building setback line.
Yard, side, means a yard extending from the front yard to the rear yard, between the side lot line and the side building setback line. In the case of corner lots, the yard along all established street right-of-way lines shall meet the requirements for front yards.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993; Ord. No. 96-01, § 2, 1-1-1996)

657:
(a) It is the intent of this section to respect established private property rights. The lawful use of any building, structure or land existing prior to the time of enactment of or subsequent amendment to the ordinance from which this article is derived may be continued subject to the regulations contained in this section.
(b) The nonconforming use of a building, structure or land shall not be changed to another nonconforming use.
(c) Any nonconforming use of a building, structure, or land which has been abandoned for a period of one year or more shall not be re-established.

(2) In the event of destruction by fire or by an act of God, shall be permitted to the full value of the building or structure.
(3) Shall be permitted to the full value of an owner-occupied dwelling.

(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
660:
The purpose of the developmental district is to establish a district on the fringe of urban growth where the predominant character of development has not yet been fully established, but where the current characteristics of use are primarily agricultural and residential. As urban growth continues, demand will grow for amendments to remove land from the development district and place it in more intensely developed zones. However, the intent of the development district is to reserve the bulk of the land for agricultural and low-density residential uses.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
664:
The purpose is to establish residential districts and to protect property in the districts from the depreciating effects of incompatible land uses. Residential uses are intended to be the primary use within each district. The residential districts are intended to preserve and protect the residential character of neighborhoods.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
666:
The purpose of the R-2 district is to establish areas in residential districts where a two-family residence will fit into and not diminish the residential character of neighborhoods.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
668:
(a) Purpose. The purpose of the R-MH district is to establish a medium- to high-density residential district and to protect property in the districts from the depreciating effects on incompatible land uses.
(b) A mobile home is a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length, or, when erected on-site, is 320 or more square feet, and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein and manufactured prior to June 15, 1976.
(c) Special districts are designed to accommodate and develop mobile home parks.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
669:
(a) State code.
(1) A structure defined by and constructed in accordance with the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, as amended, 42 USC 5401 et seq.
(2) The term "manufactured home" means a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length, or, when erected on-site, is 320 or more square feet, and which is built on a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein; except that the term "manufactured home" shall include any structure which meets all the requirements of this subsection except the size requirements, and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the secretary and complies with the standards established under this division.
(b) Manufactured homes; requirements.
(1) At least 40 percent of the roof must be double-pitched at least three in 12 or greater and covered with material that is residential in appearance, including, but not limited to, approved wood, asphalt composition shingles or fiberglass.
(2) Exterior siding cannot have a high-gloss finish and must be residential in appearance, including, but not limited to, clapboards, simulated clapboards such as conventional vinyl or metal siding, wood shingles, shakes, or similar material, but excluding smooth, ribbed, or corrugated metal or plastic panels.
(3) The home must be placed on a permanent foundation.
(4) The hitch, axles, and wheels must be removed.
(5) The unit must be oriented on the lot so that its long axis is parallel with the street.
(6) The lot must be landscaped to ensure compatibility with surrounding properties.
(c) Manufactured homes as single-family dwellings; permitted locations. Manufactured homes qualifying as dwellings, single-family, shall be allowed in all residential districts and shall be regulated uniformly with other housing constructed on-site, subject to requirements and limitations set forth in this division.
(d) Compatibility standards. Manufactured homes qualifying as dwellings, single-family, shall be compared to site-built and other housing in the immediate general area within the same zoning or residential district or area. Approval shall be granted upon the finding that the manufactured home is substantially similar or superior in size, siding material, roof material, foundation and general aesthetic appearance to site-built or other forms of housing which may be permitted in the same general area under this division.
(1) All towing devices, wheels, axles and hitches must be removed.
(2) At each exterior door, there must be a landing that is a minimum of 36 inches by 48 inches.
(e) Procedures for approval of manufactured homes classified as dwelling, single-family, other manufactured homes and mobile homes; intent. It is the intent of this section to provide procedures for approval of permits for manufactured homes classified as dwellings, single-family, other manufactured homes and mobile homes.
(1) Applications for approval of placement of manufactured homes or mobile homes shall be made on a form developed for that purpose and shall be submitted to the building inspector, who shall present said application to the planning and zoning commission for review and approval or denial, in accordance with this division.
(2) Such applications shall include all information necessary to make determinations as to conformity with the provisions of this division as applicable to each such structure and, as applicable, conformity with the standards herein, including photographs or renderings of the front and side of the manufactured home or mobile home, exterior finish, and other information necessary to make determinations required by this division.
(3) Approval or denial of the application shall be within five days of receipt of the application and all required supporting materials. The applicant shall be notified in writing of the approval, conditional approval or denial of the application within five working days after such decision is made. Conditional approval shall require that the conditions and reasons therefor be stated in writing and be agreed to by the applicant; such conditions shall be binding upon the applicant. In the case of disapproval, the reasons therefor shall be stated in writing.
(4) The building inspector may approve deviations from the definitional or compatibility standards or architectural standards set forth in subsection (b)(3), (4) or (5) of this section on the basis of a finding that the materials to be utilized or the architectural style proposed for the dwelling unit will be compatible and harmonious with or superior to existing structures in the vicinity.
(5) Appeals of the decisions of the building official in interpretations, conditional grants, or denial of permits shall be made to the city council. The decision of the city council shall be based on the purpose and intent of this division, provided that the spirit of this division shall be observed, public welfare and safety is secured, and substantial justice is done.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
672:
The P-1 district is established to provide areas for the development of structures for professional services which complement the character of adjacent districts. This district is not intended to accommodate general and highway-oriented commercial uses or residential uses, but rather to serve as a transition between more intensely developed commercial areas and residential districts.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
676:
These districts are established to provide appropriate areas for the development of commercial and service activities consistent with the existing character of commercial development. Commercial districts should have access from major traffic arteries; however, it is the intent of this division to discourage the development of long, narrow strips of commercial development fronting on major arteries, often referred to as strip commercial areas. Such strip commercial development damages the traffic-carrying capacity of streets, increases congestion, is often incompatible with adjacent residential areas, and creates disproportionate costs in the provision of government services. Extension of commercial zoning requiring amendments to this division should be made principally for the provision of planned, unified commercial areas, and not in such a way that strip commercial areas are encouraged. Extension of commercial zoning should only be made after careful consideration of compatibility with adjacent uses and whether or not other land is available which is already zoned for commercial use.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
681:
The I-1 district is intended to provide areas for industrial uses and related activities such as wholesaling, warehousing, and storage, and to protect adjacent districts from potentially harmful effects of industrial uses. This district is not intended to accommodate general commercial uses or residential uses.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
688:
(a) Corner lots. Corner lots shall be 20 percent wider that interior lots in order to meet minimum front yard requirements on all sides adjacent to a street. This includes subdivisions.
(b) Vision clearance. On any corner lot, no fence, sign, or other structure, planting, or other obstruction to vision above three feet above the established street grades shall be erected or maintained within the line connection points on the street right-of-way line 20 feet distant from the corner.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
689:
(a) Required separation between commercial and/or industrial and residential lots. When the rear or side lot line of a lot zoned and used for commercial or industrial purposes adjoins the rear or side lot line of a lot zoned or used for residential purposes, the commercial or industrial development shall comply with these requirements:
(1) The required setback line for buildings on the commercial or industrial lot shall be increased to 20 feet from the property line of the residential lot.
(2) A vision-screening buffer shall be provided along the rear or side lot line used and zoned for commercial or industrial purposes. This buffer shall consist of a vegetative, opaque screen designed to be at least six feet deep and eight feet tall at maturity, a solid wall or fence at least eight feet tall, or any combination of the above as deemed necessary by the building inspector. Such vision screening buffer shall be subject to periodic inspections by the building inspector to determine that such required walls, fences, planted dividing strips, or other types of buffers are being properly maintained in a healthy, growing condition, and are neat and orderly in appearance.
(3) These provisions shall not apply when the aforesaid side or rear lot lines do not meet due to the presence of a public street, easement, or other right-of-way greater than 25 feet in width. In such cases, said street, easement, or other rights-of-way shall be deemed as a sufficient buffer for the purposes of this article.
(b) Parking setbacks adjacent to residential uses. Parking facilities shall not be permitted in the side and rear yard setbacks for a distance of four feet from the property line for lots in residential districts.
(c) Recreational setbacks adjacent to residential uses. Outdoor recreational facilities which are adjacent to lots which are zoned or used for residential purposes shall comply with the following standards:
(1) No nonresidential pool, playground, miniature golf course, ball field, or game court shall be located closer than 50 feet from the property line of a lot zoned or used for residential purposes;
(2) No lighting shall be installed in connection with any outdoor recreational facility which is closer than 50 feet to the property line of a lot zoned or used for residential purposes, unless such lighting is of such a nature, as determined by the planning and zoning commission, that it will not be a nuisance to an adjacent residential use;
(3) A solid wall or fence, or vegetative screening which furnishes equal protection against noise and light, shall be provided when determined appropriate by the planning and zoning commission. Such vision-screening buffer shall be subject to periodic inspections by the building inspector to determine that such required walls, fences, planted dividing strips, or other types of buffers are being properly maintained in a healthy, growing condition, and are neat and orderly in appearance;
(4) No commercial activities shall be permitted in conjunction with recreational uses in residential zones except as listed below:
a. Charges and fees for use of the recreational facilities; and
b. Other activities which are directly incidental with the recreational facility and which, in the judgment of the planning and zoning commission, would not be in conflict with the residential nature of the neighborhood.
(d) Cemeteries adjacent to residential uses. Cemeteries, cemetery plots, or other facilities for the burial of the dead which are adjacent to lots which are zoned or used for residential purposes shall be no closer than 50 feet from the property line of the lot zoned or used for residential purposes. Refer to section 32-200, objectives, future land use plan.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
690:
The planning and zoning commission is authorized to hear requests for permitting special use exceptions and for conditional uses for land or structures and to recommend to the city council approval or disapproval of such applications.
(1) Requirements. A special use exception application or a conditional use application shall not be heard by the planning and zoning commission until:
a. A written application is submitted pursuant to this article which sets forth the special use exception or the conditional use being sought and the grounds on which it is requested, the location of the site, the name of the property owner, and the existing land uses within 400 feet, and other material pertinent to the request which the planning and zoning commission may require;
b. Notice of such hearing shall be posted in a conspicuous place on the property for which the special use exception or conditional use is sought by the property owner at least 15 days prior to the scheduled hearing;
c. A public hearing shall be held and shall be conducted by the planning and zoning commission. Any party may appear in person or by agent or attorney; and
d. The planning and zoning commission shall make written findings to the city council certifying compliance for the specific rules governing individual special use exceptions and conditional uses and that satisfactory provisions and arrangements have been made concerning the following, where applicable:
1. Ingress and egress to property and proposed structures thereon, with particular reference to automotive and pedestrian safety and convenience, traffic flow and control, access in case of fire and catastrophe.
2. Off-street parking and loading areas, where required.
3. Refuse collection areas and availability of utilities.
4. Signs, if any, and proposed exterior lighting with reference to glare, traffic safety, and harmony of properties in the district.
5. Required building setbacks.
6. General compatibility with adjacent properties and other property in the district.
(2) Validity of plan. All approved plans, conditions, restrictions, and rules, made part of the approval of the planning and zoning commission and the city council, if approved by the council, shall constitute certification on the part of the applicant that the proposed use shall conform to such regulations.
(3) Time limit. All applications for special use exceptions and for conditional uses shall be decided within 45 days of the date of application. The applicant shall be provided with written notice of either approval or denial.
(4) Public hearing. Prior to taking action on any request for a special use exception permit or conditional use permit, the planning and zoning commission shall hold a public hearing. The procedures for advertising and holding the public hearing shall be as provided in article V of this chapter, except that the planning and zoning commission shall conduct the hearing.
(5) Use restrictions. In recommending approval to the city council, the planning and zoning commission may impose such conditions regarding the location, character, or other features of the proposed uses for buildings, including the placement and types of signs, as it may deem advisable and necessary in the furtherance of the general purposes of the city zoning ordinance; and in the exercise of its approval, the city council may impose such conditions regarding the locations, character, or other features of the proposed uses for buildings, including the placement and types of signs, as it may deem advisable and necessary in the furtherance of the general purposes of the city zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993; Ord. No. 96-01, § 3, 1-1-1996)
693:
This article is intended to permit greater flexibility in the development of residential areas and establish a review process by the planning and zoning commission for such development plans.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), § 11-4.1, 2-2-1993)
695:
The minimum size of any tract zoned and developed as a planned unit development (PUD) shall be five acres. Such PUD shall also have permanent, paved access to a public road.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), § 11-4.3, 2-2-1993)
696:
(a) A maximum of five percent of the total area of the development may be devoted to commercial, retail, or professional uses.
(b) A maximum of 75 percent of the remaining (non-commercial) area of the development shall be devoted to recreational and/or open spaces. This percentage may include public and semi-public buildings, recreational facilities and buildings, and common open spaces.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), § 11-4.4, 2-2-1993)
697:
(a) Street access. Any building established in connection with a PUD that cannot properly be served by emergency or service vehicles from an abutting street shall be made accessible to such vehicles by a paved driveway with a width of not less than 20 feet, exclusive of parking space.
(b) Off-street parking. Off-street parking facilities established in connection with a PUD shall be of such a design that it will not interfere with the safe movement of pedestrians, the efficient flow of traffic, and the access of service and delivery vehicles. The requirements for off-street parking for uses in a PUD shall follow the requirements set forth in section 32-201.
(c) Separation within development. All buildings within a PUD shall be a least 20 feet apart, but at least 40 feet apart when front-to-front.
(d) Building length. In residential buildings, no single row of dwelling units which are physically attached shall be greater than 200 feet in length.
(e) Setback requirements. There shall be no minimum lot size, no minimum setbacks, and no minimum lot widths within the PUD; provided, however, that measures are taken to provide reasonable visual and acoustical privacy for dwelling units. There shall be provided a minimum ten-foot buffer between any PUD and adjacent residential areas. Further, each dwelling unit shall have access to a street, walkway, or other common area, and no structure or building shall be erected within 15 feet of any other structures.
(f) Water, sewerage, and drainage. Adequate provisions for water supply, sanitary sewerage, and storm drainage shall be installed by the developer in accordance with accepted engineering principles.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), § 11-4.5, 2-2-1993)
701:
The provisions of this chapter shall be administered and enforced by the building inspector of the city, or his delegated representatives, who is hereby given the authority to perform these functions. His duties shall include receiving applications, inspecting premises, and issuing building permits and certificates of occupancy for uses and structures that meet the requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
702:
The violation of any provision of this chapter shall constitute a misdemeanor, and any person, firm, corporation, or agent who shall in any manner violate any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof, shall be punished in the discretion of the court. Each day such violation of this chapter shall continue shall be deemed as a separate offense.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
703:
(a) Establishment of a planning and zoning commission. A planning and zoning commission is hereby established to hear appeals and recommend action to the city council for variances from the terms of this chapter.
(b) Membership and terms of office. The planning and zoning commission shall consist of five members appointed by the mayor and council. Members appointed to the planning and zoning commission shall hold no other public office. All members shall be qualified electors of the city. The members shall serve for overlapping terms of four years, except for their initial appointments, in which three members shall be appointed for initial terms of four years and two members shall be appointed for three-year terms of office. Planning and zoning commission members may be appointed to succeed themselves, and for terms of four years.
(c) Vacancy. Vacancies shall be filled for unexpired terms. A vacancy in a term of office shall occur whenever the mayor and council finds that a member has resigned, or when the mayor and council shall have dismissed a member because of his repeated failure to attend meetings of the planning and zoning commission without just cause or because the member has been guilty of malfeasance or misconduct in office.
(d) Organization. The planning and zoning commission shall hold an annual organizational meeting and shall elect a chairperson and vice-chairperson from among its members before proceeding to any other matters of business. The planning and zoning commission shall meet at the call of the chairperson and shall designate the time and place of its meetings. The planning and zoning commission shall adopt its own rules of procedure and keep a record of its proceedings in accordance with the state statutes and these regulations. Newly appointed members shall be installed at the first regular meeting after their appointment.
(e) Meetings and quorum. Three members of the planning and zoning commission shall constitute a quorum for the conduct of business. The members of the planning and zoning commission shall regularly attend meetings and public hearings of the planning and zoning commission and shall serve without compensation, except for reimbursement for authorized expenses attendant to the performance of their duties.
(f) Functions of the planning and zoning commission. The planning and zoning commission shall have the following powers:
(1) To hear appeals where it is alleged by the appellant that there is an error in any order requirement permit, decision, determination, or refusal made by the building inspector or other administrative official in the carrying out of enforcement of any provisions of this chapter.
(2) To hear requests for the interpretation of the official zoning map and for any special questions upon which the planning and zoning commission is authorized to pass.
(3) To hear and recommend action to the city council for variances from the terms of this chapter, and other actions related to the enforcement of these regulations.
(g) Appeals to the planning and zoning commission. An appeal to the planning and zoning commission may be taken by any person, firm, or corporation aggrieved by any decision of the building inspector based in whole or in part on the provisions of this chapter. Such appeal shall be filed in writing with the planning and zoning commission and the building inspector shall transmit to the planning and zoning commission all documentation related to the case under appeal. The planning and zoning commission shall set a reasonable time for the public hearing of the appeal and the building inspector shall place a sign conspicuously on the property, at least 15 days prior to the public hearing, giving notice of the public hearing.
(h) Variances. The planning and zoning commission may recommend to the city council that a variance from the terms of this chapter be granted in such cases that the variance will not be contrary to the public interest where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of this chapter would result in unnecessary hardship. A variance from the terms of this chapter shall not be granted by the planning and zoning commission unless and until:
(1) There are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular parcel of property in question because of its size, shape, or topography;
(2) The application of this chapter to this particular piece of property would create an unnecessary hardship;
(3) Such conditions are peculiar to the particular piece of property involved;
(4) Relief, if granted, would not cause substantial detriment to the public good or impair the purposes and intent of this chapter or the current map for the city.
(i) Action on appeals and variances. In exercising its powers, the planning and zoning commission shall, in conformity with the provisions of this chapter, recommend to the city council that it may reverse or affirm, wholly or partly, or may modify the order, requirement, decision, or determination as ought to be made.
(j) Further appeals. Any persons jointly or severally aggrieved by any decision of the planning and zoning commission and the mayor and city council relating to the regulations set forth in this chapter may present to the superior court in and for the county, a petition setting forth that a decision of the planning and zoning commission or mayor and city council is illegal, in whole or in part, specifying the grounds of the illegality. Such petition shall be presented to the court within 30 days after the date of the filing of the decision.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
704:
The mayor and city council shall establish a schedule of fees for building permit applications, zoning change applications, zoning map amendment applications, and zoning variance applications. The schedule of fees shall be posted in the office of the building inspector and may be altered and amended only by the mayor and city council.
(Ord. No. 1993-02(1), 2-2-1993)
